name: Got You
tagline: You only play jokes on the people you want to keep.
epigraph: Built on Chicago's bitter liqueur for willing visitors. The face they pull has a name.
language_row: Wren's 4-gram runs (the lint's own `ngrams()`) against every pour: clean after eleven fixes in v1 and three more in v2 (among them *outlaw-regular-guy*'s "know exactly where the line", *outlaw-explorer*'s "years later he said", *ruler-caregiver*'s "the science of cocktails"). Never "invitation", "ignored" or "everyone says it" (the Trickster's, *For Kicks*'); no "lad", "cheeky chappie", "lovable rogue"; never "shot", "down it" or "punishing" as a dare; "dared" only of Sam, the source's verb. "he"/"his" only for Sam Mechling (lint warnings accepted by Wren). "Straight" kept out of the closing line (bar talk for neat). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/jeppsons-malort-sam-mechling.md`: *Oxford Companion to Spirits and Cocktails*, JEPPSON'S MALÖRT (pdf 1103, Jeff Ruby) and SALT (pdf 1721); Adriana Cardona-Maguigad, "The unlikely rise of Malört as Chicago's drink", WBEZ *Curious City*, 6 Jul 2023; Claire McNear, *The Ringer*, 6 Feb 2019; Melissa McEwen, NPR *The Salt*, Apr 2013; the maker's product page (35%); Geoff Kleinman, *Drink Spirits* review, 2012 (grapefruit peel notes, colour); 27 CFR 5.150 (US liqueur sugar floor). Craft: Dave Arnold, *Liquid Intelligence* pp. 126, 149 (the Shaken Drake); *Cocktail Codex* pp. 118, 120, 133; *The Flavor Matrix* pdf 263. Audits: `work/regular-guy-jester/historian-audit-v1.md`, `-v2.md`. Room notes: `work/regular-guy-jester/`.
names_note: **Got You**, the room's pick (all three, r4): how every prank ends, and "I've got you", the plain, joke-free sentence y5 asks for. *Ask a Local* was Tomás's pick in r3 (the newcomer's line; *The Ringer*'s visitors who "trusted a Chicagoan to order for them"), conceded in r4: it carries only the first half and brushes *Brought Home*. Also considered: *One of Us* (trips the one-voice check), *Your Turn* (the next person's), *Got You Back* (repeats y5), *The Letter* (captions the story), *Dared* (aims the source's verb at the guest).
open_items: **The plan's lead overturned:** the 1874 Tom Collins hoax (plans/regular-guy.md) fails Wren's let-in test: its target walks from bar to bar alone, "steaming", while everyone else is in on it (*Imbibe!* pdf 82). The room chose Malört and Sam Mechling; the Collins/Old Tom/highball reservation is released for the family.

**Years kept out:** WBEZ puts the dare in the late 2000s and the meeting "around 2012"; *The Ringer* has 2011 for the comedy show. The letter and the cheque are WBEZ's alone, told plainly. Josh Noel, *Malört* (Chicago Review Press, 2024) would settle both: a library gap.

**The label:** 35% from the maker's page; no sugar figure published, so modelled at the US liqueur floor (2.4 g/100 ml, 27 CFR 5.150); colour (FD&C Yellow No. 5) from a 2012 review. The current label is unseen by Hester.
**Abroad:** no confirmed retailer outside the US; the substitute is a Swedish besk (beskbrännvin) of 35% or stronger.

**Balance, freeform:** 16.8% / 9.62 g / 1.150%: sugar and acid above the shaken band, as Arnold's own Shaken Drake (15.6 / 10.2 / 1.03, *LI* p. 149); justified in Checks. 20 ml of stray melt reads 14.5%, hence "serve at once".

**The spark is a reviewer's palate:** Kleinman's "clear grapefruit peel notes" in Malört (2012), and the aspirin-in-grapefruit-peel description Sam counted among his favourites (*The Ringer*); never a property of the bottle.

**Dossier only:** Carl Jeppson, Prohibition and the medicine; the birthday-shot prank; D.C.; the comedy nights; "nearly a decade"; Gabelick's own taste (sources contradict); Brode's label line; the name "Malört face" never credited to Sam.
**History share:** 56% raw, 48% without y3's signposted reading (Wren). Noted for Robin.
